# CEO Plan: User Dashboard Page
Generated by /plan-ceo-review (via /autoplan) on 2026-09-10
Branch: main | Mode: SELECTIVE EXPANSION
Repo: gstack-autoplan-chain-9599im (fixture; no remote)

## Baseline scope (unchanged from the source plan)
- `/dashboard` page rendered after login, with three panels: QuickActions, NotificationsPanel, ActivityFeed
- One aggregate endpoint `GET /api/dashboard` returning a top-level `fetchedAt` (server time of the response) plus one result per panel (`{ ok: true, data } | { ok: false, error }`), so one panel failing never blanks the page
- "Mark all as read" behind a confirm dialog built on the existing dialog primitive
- A toast primitive (new, built as a shared app-level component, success feedback only)
- Canonical panel states, used everywhere in this record: LOADING (skeleton), EMPTY, ERROR, SUCCESS, REFRESHING (a SUCCESS or EMPTY panel re-fetching while its previous content stays visible). A shared `PanelFrame` component owns the chrome for all five; each panel supplies only its SUCCESS rendering.
- Tailwind tokens; mobile-first sm/md/lg
- Out of scope, from the source plan: dark mode, personalization (separate plans)

## Vision

### North star (12-month direction, NOT this release)
The dashboard that already knows what you were doing. The hero is the one eligible
"resume" action, huge and one Tab away. Notifications are ranked by urgency and can be
cleared per item. Activity streams in live. Nothing the member needs after login is
more than one click away, and nothing they don't need takes up space.

### 10x within this release's constraints
The source plan forbids new mutation APIs and new infrastructure, so per-item read and
live streaming are deferred (E9 below, and the per-item read API in the deferred list).
The 10x lever available now is hierarchy: QuickActions first, Notifications second,
Activity third, at every breakpoint. The per-panel result envelope and the shared
`PanelFrame` are the widget contract that lets every later panel plug in without
re-deciding its states.

## Scope Decisions

| # | Proposal | Effort | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| E1 | "Updated Xm ago" + Refresh in page header | S | ACCEPTED | Uses the top-level `fetchedAt` of the aggregate response; Refresh puts panels into REFRESHING; makes staleness visible |
| E2 | Notification rows deep-link to their target | S | ACCEPTED | Route targets exist per contracts; link only. The row stays unread after the member returns, until "Mark all as read" (intentional: no per-item read API in this release) |
| E3 | `<time datetime>` relative + absolute-on-hover timestamps | S | ACCEPTED | Accessibility policy; trivial |
| E4 | "View all" links per panel into existing full pages | S | ACCEPTED | Existing pages own older-page navigation |
| E5 | Optimistic mark-all-read with rollback | S | ACCEPTED | Idempotent snapshot-bounded API makes it safe; on failure the unread markers are restored and an error message renders inline inside the notifications panel (persistent, screen-reader visible); the toast is used for success only |
| E6 | Keyboard shortcut to first quick action | S | DEFERRED | Single-key shortcuts need a11y design first |
| E7 | Unread badge in global nav | M | DEFERRED | Outside blast radius (global nav) |
| E8 | Smart post-login redirect experiment cohort | M | DEFERRED | Run after the cohort metric is read |
| E9 | Real-time updates (SSE) | L | DEFERRED | New infrastructure |
| E10 | Six named client analytics events | S | ACCEPTED | The source plan's contracts require "exposure and interaction instrumentation" in general; this decision names the concrete events (listed below) |

## Accepted Scope (added to this plan)
- Page header with "Updated Xm ago" (from the aggregate response's top-level `fetchedAt`) and a Refresh control that moves panels to REFRESHING without clearing content
- Notification rows link to their target route when one is present; the row remains unread until "Mark all as read"
- `<time datetime>` timestamps, relative text with absolute on hover
- "View all activity" and "View all notifications" links into the existing pages
- Optimistic mark-all-read with full rollback; failure message inline in the panel, success via toast
- Client analytics events: dashboard_viewed, dashboard_panel_state (ERROR/EMPTY only), dashboard_quick_action_clicked, dashboard_mark_all_read, dashboard_view_all_clicked, dashboard_refresh_clicked

## Deferred to TODOS.md
All deferrals wait until the cohort metric has been read against control (see Gate below), then:
- Unread badge in global nav (P2)
- Smart-redirect experiment cohort for single-action members (P2)
- Real-time notification/activity updates via SSE (P3, infra decision)
- Keyboard shortcut to first quick action (P3, after a11y review)
- QuickActions predicate cache, 30s per member, only if measured p95 > 300 ms (P3)
- Retire the `dashboard_landing` feature flag after 100% rollout (P2)
- Per-item mark-read / undo API, which would allow direct action instead of the confirm modal (P3, product decision)

## Alternatives considered
- A: Smart redirect + QuickActions strip (completeness 4/10): fastest to the resume action but drops alerts and activity, two of the three post-login jobs.
- B: Dashboard + per-panel envelope + shared primitives (9/10): **decided** (provisionally; the /autoplan final approval gate may override to B').
- B': B with three parallel client calls instead of one aggregate (8/10): free isolation, but three round-trips and three auth checks on the hottest page, and quick actions need a new endpoint anyway. Revisit after launch only if aggregate p95 exceeds 300 ms for two consecutive rollout stages.
- C: B + real-time + per-item read + nav badge (9/10 but out of scope): violates the plan's no-new-mutation-API and no-new-infra constraints.

## Rollout mechanism, stages and gates
- Mechanism: feature flag `dashboard_landing`. Flag on: post-login redirect goes to `/dashboard` and the route renders. Flag off: post-login redirect goes to the current landing page and a direct request to `/dashboard` redirects there too, so control members cannot reach the dashboard and the comparison is uncontaminated. Members with the flag on are the "cohort"; members with it off are the "control". Rollback at any time is flag off.
- Metric: "login → first completed task" is the time from the existing `login` analytics event to the first `action_complete` event for the same member in the same session. Sessions with no `action_complete` within 30 minutes are counted as not completed: they feed the completed-task-rate guardrail and are excluded from the timing distribution. Baseline p50 and p90 are pulled from existing analytics events before any production cohort.
- Success: cohort p50 ≤ 45 s AND cohort p50 ≤ control p50 AND cohort p90 ≤ control p90. If the measured control p50 is already below 45 s, the success bar becomes cohort p50 ≤ 0.85 × control p50 instead of the absolute 45 s.
- Stages: staging soak, all internal members, 3 days, exit only with zero 5xx and panel error rate < 1%. Production 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%. Advance a stage only after ≥ 3 days AND ≥ 500 cohort dashboard logins, with no guardrail breach. The cohort metric is first read at the end of the 25% stage; advancing to 50% requires the success condition to hold at that read, and 100% requires it to hold again at the 50% read.
- Prerequisite (asserted before staging soak): the existing `action_complete` event is emitted by all three registry actions (create item, resume assigned work, invite member). If any is missing, adding it is a blocking prerequisite task.
- Guardrails, each evaluated only when its window holds ≥ 200 cohort requests (at 5% this may mean a 60-minute window): cohort completed-task rate more than 5% relative below control over the same rolling 24 h; cohort permission-error rate more than 2 percentage points above control over the same rolling 24 h; any panel `ok:false` rate > 5% over 10 minutes; endpoint p95 > 600 ms over 10 minutes. A breach pages on-call and the flag is turned off manually within 15 minutes. If the existing flag service already supports alert-driven kill switches, wire the breach to it; no new automation infrastructure is built for this plan.
- Latency remedies, in order: if endpoint p95 > 300 ms for two consecutive stages, first add the per-member predicate cache (a performance fix, exempt from the feature gate below); if still over, switch to alternative B' (three parallel calls). The 600 ms guardrail is separate and triggers rollback, not remediation.
- Gate: no new dashboard features (including the separately planned dark mode and personalization) until the cohort metric has been read against control at the 25% stage. Performance remediation is exempt from this gate.
- Refresh semantics: SUCCESS and EMPTY panels enter REFRESHING (content stays visible); an ERROR panel returns to LOADING on Refresh or Retry.

## Spec review record
Three adversarial review rounds (scores 7/10 → 8/10 → 8/10; 21 issues raised, 21 fixed in-document). The loop hit its 3-iteration cap with the round-3 issues fixed inline above; no unresolved reviewer concerns remain.
